authoring: Direct conversational research and Korean authoring. No external LLM API and no generated scientific-content script.
scope_convention: reference_section means the specified returned passages, not an assertion that the entire article was read. publisher_abstract includes the original author's repository abstract. stored_search_excerpt preserves primary publisher text retrieved through search when direct access failed.
comparison: Compared against previously read canonical physical principles and candidate-specific key/title/principle searches across all current groups, including chemistry and information. Current catalog had 1740 entries at structural validation. Explicit nearest mechanisms and boundaries appear in each authored row. Key-existence checks do not by themselves establish semantic novelty.

evidence.read: Original 2019 experiment: abstract, Q(T) for TED, Q for Phonon-Phonon Scattering, and discussion of frequency and temperature scaling.
evidence.quote: the stresses induce distortion of the phonon energy spectrum away from the equilibrium Boltzmann distribution
evidence.support: Local distribution relaxation through phonon scattering adds entropy. The paper separates it from spatial temperature-gradient heat flow and defines the regime by the acoustic period exceeding thermal-phonon relaxation time. Experiment distinguishes competing damping by geometry and frequency scaling.
evidence.limitation: Silicon MEMS evidence does not provide a universal damping constant. Landau-Rumer and Akhiezer frequency regimes are not counted as separate new cards. The paper's historical attribution date is not used.

evidence.read: Publisher-indexed abstract of Argon 1979 returned by search; direct ScienceDirect open failed. Abstract describes thermally activated local shear transformations, two temperature regimes, free-volume model and plastic localization.
evidence.quote: thermally activated shear transformations initiated around free volume regions under an applied shear stress
evidence.support: Localized atomic rearrangements produce plastic shear in a glass without requiring crystalline dislocation glide. Both temperature regimes are one mechanism.
evidence.limitation: This is a model, not a direct image of predetermined defects. The exact region size and a universal free-volume criterion are deliberately omitted. The card differentiates local events from macroscopic thermal-softening feedback.

evidence.read: Publisher-indexed abstract of Cahn, Mishin and Suzuki 2006; direct page retrieval failed. Original MD study of copper tilt grain boundaries.
evidence.quote: normal grain boundary (GB) motion must often be coupled to tangential translation of grains
evidence.support: Boundary-normal migration produces shear deformation, and conversely shear stress drives normal motion. Coupling factor depends on misorientation and temperature.

supplement.read: Introduction and Results around geometric coupling factor beta = tangential translation / normal displacement.
supplement.support: Original tungsten simulation explicitly contrasts coupled migration with pure grain-boundary sliding. Unusual shuffle modes are not additional cards. Later comments on the page are not substituted for the published Results.

evidence.limitation: The primary abstract supports the coupled geometric mechanism; the row does not claim a single universal disconnection type or atomic shuffle path.

evidence.read: Original Granato-Lucke 1956 publisher PDF endpoint redirected to AIP/Silverchair article-minimal/161648. Returned content was the publisher abstract and references, not PDF full text.
evidence.quote: a pinned dislocation loop oscillating under the influence of an applied stress
evidence.support: The original theory gives damping and modulus change, with frequency-dependent and hysteretic losses from the pinned-line model. Both remain one card.
evidence.limitation: No microscopic drag coefficient or particular breakaway law is inferred from the abstract. The new row concerns oscillatory loss rather than Frank-Read multiplication.

evidence.read: Original 2018 dislocation-dynamics study: Results precipitate-obstacle cases, Figure 3 caption and Discussion on classical loops versus twisted nooses.
evidence.quote: dislocations bypass the precipitates by bowing around them and forming Orowan loops
evidence.support: The advancing line leaves loops around obstacles. It is a specific pathway beneath broad precipitation strengthening, distinct from cutting, climb, and a repeating Frank-Read source.
evidence.limitation: Simulation evidence in iron, not direct observation in all alloys. The atypical nonplanar noose is retained as a condition and not split into a material-specific new mechanism.

evidence.read: Original Rempel-Meyer 2019 theory: abstract, premelting/effective-stress derivation and concluding discussion.
evidence.quote: melting on their upstream sides and refreezing downstream
evidence.support: The paper separates liquid pressure from ice pressure; their difference alters melting equilibrium. Premelt liquid transport and latent-heat conduction enable passage over obstacles. Effective-stress forcing is stronger than equal hydrostatic changes in both phases.
evidence.limitation: Do not equate the effect with universal negative Clapeyron slope. The paper explicitly extends effective-stress-driven melt/refreeze cycling to solids wetted by their own melt. Pressure solution instead transports solute in another solvent.

evidence.read: Original-author 2023 numerical control study: abstract, Introduction on second-principal-axis instability and Methods rotational equation (7).
evidence.quote: unstable rotation around the direction close to the body’s second principal axis
evidence.support: Torque-free angular-momentum conservation gives coupled Euler rotation; the intermediate principal axis is unstable. The paper uses changing inertia to initiate and control flips.
evidence.limitation: The card takes the fixed-inertia limit of the stated equation, an explicit inference. It does not count inertia-control engineering as a second effect and does not repeat the article's overly broad phrase about generic chaos in fixed rigid-body rotation.

evidence.read: Original-author version 2 (2017): abstract, Introduction, section 2 prototypical rattleback equations and Figure 1 caption on spin/pitch/roll energy exchange.
evidence.support: Principal inertia and contact-curvature directions are skew. Nonlinear spin, pitch and roll coupling produces unequal reversal time scales, including reversals in either sense in the ideal model.
evidence.limitation: Contact-constrained body, not a torque-free top. No perpetual motion or angular-momentum violation. Dissipation and slipping can suppress ideal repeated reversals.

evidence.read: Original-author JMPS 2018 manuscript: abstract, Introduction paragraph on energy input, and Conclusions on measured flutter/divergence and damping effects.
evidence.quote: follower forces can in certain circumstances provide energy to the elastic system
evidence.support: A tangential force maintained by a wheel and conveyor validates follower loading experimentally. Increasing oscillatory amplitude precedes static divergence in the tested regime. Damping can lower the flutter threshold.
evidence.limitation: Positive cyclic work and instability are conditional, not claims for every follower load. Ziegler damping destabilization is kept in this card's conditions rather than separately counted.

evidence.read: Original 2020 experiment: abstract, Introduction and Results/Theoretical model, Lorentz transformation and drag-phase equation (1).
evidence.quote: applying Lorentz transformation to the coupling system
evidence.support: A microcavity translates along the coupling fibre; moving-medium propagation alters phase. Normal and anomalous dispersion alter the dragging coefficient. Translation establishes the boundary from Sagnac rotation.
evidence.limitation: Brillouin transparency/absorption provide dispersion enhancement here; they are not new cards. The effect does not alter vacuum light speed or establish faster-than-light signalling.

evidence.read: Original-author 2005 paper: abstract, Introduction, section VII A discussions of successive boosts and noncommutativity, printed pages 23-24.
evidence.quote: not a pure boost but rather is the product of a boost and a rotation
evidence.support: A rapidity-space derivation from Lorentz invariance links finite non-collinear boost rotation and its continuous Thomas-precession limit.

supplement.support: Original letter states that relativistic kinematics resolves the factor-of-two spin-precession discrepancy. Its abstract does not itself derive non-collinear boost composition, so the row uses the accessible original-author theoretical treatment.

evidence.limitation: This is kinematic reference-frame rotation; it is not a new force and does not imply an observed spin-rotation measurement in this paper.

evidence.read: Original Fernando et al. 1997 publisher abstract returned in search, including mean-field approximation and upper-bound caveat.
evidence.quote: intraatomic Coulomb repulsion of itinerant electrons provides another Stoner mechanism of band splitting
evidence.support: Repulsive itinerant-electron correlations can favour spin-split ferromagnetic states. The primary model explicitly distinguishes the mean-field approximation from exact magnetic moments.
evidence.limitation: No claim that this criterion guarantees actual ordering in every dimension. Early ultracold-gas observations with competing molecular decay were not used as an unqualified experimental demonstration.

evidence.read: Bruno 1989 original PDF: abstract, section II A spin-orbit term, and sections III B/IV relation of anisotropy, crystal field, band filling and orbital moment.
evidence.quote: The spin-orbit coupling, responsible for the magnetocrystalline anisotropy
evidence.support: The perturbative calculation gives directional energy differences from spin-orbit coupling of crystal-field-defined orbitals. Predictions depend on the orbital occupation and crystal-field splitting.
evidence.limitation: The source model overestimates some measured coefficients. Directional energy is the mechanism; no universal easy-axis sign, coefficient, or proportionality is asserted. Shape demagnetization is a different contribution.

evidence.read: Original 2020 measurements and modelling: abstract, Introduction, Results discussion following inelastic-scattering evidence and double-well model.
evidence.quote: phonons being overdamped by resonant scattering with the tunneling states
evidence.support: A structural atom in a shallow double well provides a quantum two-level system that resonantly scatters heat-bearing phonons. The paper explicitly relates this to the general glass tunneling model while showing a higher-frequency crystal example.

supplement.support: The ionic-tunneling theory explains low-temperature glass heat capacity, thermal conductivity and anomalous phonon free path. The new card remains one structural-tunneling scattering mechanism across glass and crystal cases.

evidence.limitation: The measured crystal is BaTiS3. High-temperature applicability requires sufficiently high tunneling splitting; it is not generalized to arbitrary glasses or all low-conductivity solids.

evidence.read: Original 2016 ESR experiment: discussion of Figure 2 carrier susceptibility, Figure 3 energy/spin states and Figure 4 weak temperature dependence.
evidence.quote: reflects the density of states at the Fermi surface
evidence.support: Carrier spin susceptibility tracks Fermi-surface density of states and is weakly temperature dependent in the observed degenerate regime. Localized vacancy-spin response is separately fitted.
evidence.limitation: The spin-occupation explanation is the physical interpretation of these Fermi-degenerate-state results, not a new measurement in every metal. Interactions, band edges and strong fields can invalidate constant-susceptibility simplification.

exclusions.reason: Existing principle already explicitly says misaligned pressure and density gradients generate vorticity. A broader-flow wording would duplicate the stated microscopic source term.

Cahn impurity-drag mechanism is credible, but proposed wording was diffusion/segregation-retarded motion of a defect, already present for dislocations. Changing defect dimension alone was not judged enough here.

source.read: Publisher-selected original Cahn paper abstract; dependence on boundary velocity, impurity diffusivity and binding.

exclusions.candidate: separate Landau-Rumer damping / BCC twisted-noose Orowan bypass / Ziegler paradox
exclusions.reason: Frequency, host-specific glide geometry, or damping-conditioned regimes remain within the corresponding authored pathway rather than becoming extra cards.

parent_cross_review.recommendation: Merge the two direct thermal-use cards into a generalized reaction-enthalpy card while preserving reversible versus single-use and reaction-specific constraints. Parent reports merge completed.
parent_cross_review.reason: Existing hydration conditions already called it the same principle as reversible thermochemical storage. Both current card principles only describe reaction enthalpy heating or temperature-rise delay. Dehydration source discusses steam dilution and residue barrier too, but those were explicitly outside the existing card; they cannot retroactively justify a different counted path.

sources.support: Microcalorimetric hydration and firing/temperature-dependent kinetics; no independently described non-enthalpic heating mechanism.
